candidates.content_text:
Who we are
The City of Salisbury is the most progressive council in South Australia, driving growth, jobs, housing and opportunity in the north. With a workforce of over 400 people, we offer the chance to collaborate with teams across the organisation to deliver meaningful, community-focused projects.
The City Infrastructure Department delivers asset management, capital works, and maintenance programs, as well as oversees lease management for local community and sporting clubs, and security and civil compliance functions.
Join us and see the positive impact your work can make.
About the role
The City of Salisbury is seeking three experienced Asset Engineers to join the Engineering Assets & Systems team within City Infrastructure. Opportunities are available across Civil, Roads and Drainage asset portfolios.
Reporting to the Divisional Head, Engineering Assets & Systems (Asset Engineer - Civil and Asset Engineer - Roads) or the Senior Stormwater Engineer (Asset Engineer - Drainage), you will be responsible for developing, maintaining and improving asset management plans, undertaking engineering investigations and modelling, and supporting long-term infrastructure planning and investment decisions.
You will play a key role in managing and improving some of the City's most important infrastructure assets, including roads, drainage networks, wetlands, bridges, boardwalks, coastal assets, carparks, signage and stormwater infrastructure, helping ensure they continue to meet the needs of our growing community.
Your key responsibilities will include
- Develop, maintain and improve Asset Management Plans across a range of infrastructure asset classes.
- Undertake engineering investigations, modelling, analysis and reporting to support asset management decisions.
- Develop capital renewal, maintenance and lifecycle programs.
- Assess asset condition, risk, service levels and long-term investment priorities.
- Prepare project briefs and business cases for infrastructure projects and renewal programs.
- Evaluate consultant reports, designs and technical proposals.
- Provide specialist engineering and asset management advice across the organisation.
- Support planning for future growth and infrastructure needs across the city.
- Build and maintain effective working relationships with community members, developers, government agencies, service authorities and internal stakeholders.
- Communicate technical information and asset management recommendations clearly to a diverse range of stakeholders, including residents, elected members and senior leaders.
- Respond to enquiries from residents, elected members and other stakeholders.
About you
You are a qualified engineer with experience in infrastructure asset management and a passion for delivering practical, long-term outcomes for communities. You combine strong technical capability with excellent communication skills and can confidently engage with a wide range of stakeholders. You are able to translate complex engineering and asset management information into clear, practical advice that supports informed decision-making.
You will also have
- Degree qualifications in Civil Engineering, equivalent qualifications, or proven extensive experience in asset management relating to civil infrastructure and stormwater.
- Experience in infrastructure asset management, planning and lifecycle analysis.
- Knowledge of asset management frameworks such as ISO 55000 and IIMM/IPWEA practices.
- Experience using asset management, GIS and engineering modelling systems.
- Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Proven experience building productive relationships with a diverse range of internal and external stakeholders.
- Strong written communication skills, including the preparation of reports, business cases and technical documentation.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage competing priorities.
- Current driver's licence.
Desirable
- Postgraduate qualifications in asset management.
- Experience working within local government.
What we offer
- State-of-the-art Salisbury Community Hub is 25 minutes from the CBD with excellent rail and road connections.
- Modern and positive work environments.
- Free car parking.
- Flexible work options.
- Three additional leave days per year.
- Annual pay rises.
- Health and wellbeing programs, including skin checks, health assessments, flu vaccinations and an employee assistance program.
- Professional development opportunities.

Read the Asset Engineer (Roads) [Position Description].
Read the Asset Engineer (Drainage) [Position Description]. 
Eligibility 
A National Police Clearance, or the willingness and ability to obtain one, is a requirement of the recruitment and selection process.
We are committed to creating a safe, inclusive and diverse workplace where everyone feels valued and respected. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds and experiences, including Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds, people with disability, veterans, and members of the LGBTQIA+ community.

All enquiries can be made to employment@salisbury.sa.gov.au
Applications close 9:00am, 25 November 2026.

Graduate Civil Engineer | Property & Infrastructure
Adelaide | Graduate Opportunity
- Build your civil engineering capability through supervised, hands-on project work

The Opportunity
Start your engineering career by contributing to practical civil solutions for property and infrastructure projects.
Reporting to the Section Manager, you'll support the preparation of civil engineering designs, drawings, calculations, documentation and specifications. Working under the guidance of experienced engineers, you'll develop your technical capability while contributing to defined components of broader projects in the office and field.
You'll gain exposure to concept, feasibility and detailed design work, including stormwater drainage, erosion control and crossings for waterways, pipelines, rail and roads. You'll also collaborate with project engineers and multidisciplinary teams across Fyfe, building a strong foundation for your engineering career.
The Impact You'll Have
- Contribute to civil engineering calculations, drawings and designs for property and infrastructure projects.
- Support concept, feasibility and detailed design documentation, incorporating technical feedback and progressing work through the required reviews.
- Help prepare construction scopes, project specifications, services reviews, quantity estimates and opinions of probable cost.
- Participate in project meetings and supervised site inspections involving clients, contractors, councils and regulatory authorities.
- Strengthen project delivery by maintaining accurate records, communicating progress and completing assigned work to agreed timeframes, quality standards and budgets.
- Support safe, high-quality outcomes by applying relevant Australian Standards, engineering codes, Fyfe's quality system and applicable WHS requirements under supervision.
What You'll Bring
You'll bring a strong foundation in civil engineering, an eagerness to learn and the motivation to develop through practical project experience.
- Tertiary qualifications in Civil Engineering.
- A foundational understanding of civil engineering principles and relevant Australian Standards, guides and engineering codes.
- High computer literacy and a willingness to develop your capability in relevant civil engineering software and project systems.
- Sound mathematical, logical and analytical skills, with developing technical report-writing capability.
- Effective written communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to contribute positively to multidisciplinary teams.
- The ability to organise assigned tasks, work to agreed timeframes and quality standards, and communicate when guidance or support is required.
- Australian citizenship or permanent residency.
Exposure to property and infrastructure projects through university study, placements or work experience would be viewed favourably.
Why Fyfe?
Fyfe is an Australian multidisciplinary consultancy specialising in engineering, environment, planning and surveying. We partner with clients across Energy & Resources, Renewables, Infrastructure and Property, delivering practical solutions that support the energy transition and critical infrastructure projects shaping Australia's future.
In this role, you'll have the opportunity to:
- Build practical civil engineering experience across varied property and infrastructure projects.
- Learn directly from experienced engineers through supervised assignments, regular feedback and technical review.
- Work with national multidisciplinary teams and see how different technical capabilities come together.
- Develop experience across design, documentation, project coordination and supervised site activities.
- Contribute to client-focused project delivery while building the technical and professional capability to take on broader responsibilities over time.
Interested?
If you're ready to turn your civil engineering studies into practical project experience and build your career with an experienced multidisciplinary team, we'd like to hear from you.
Join Fyfe and help deliver high-quality civil engineering solutions for property and infrastructure projects.
Only candidates who are Australian Citizens, Permanent Residents or hold full Australian working rights will be considered.
Agency applications will not be accepted.

- Sound understanding of civil engineering design principles, technical standards and documentation requirements.
- Experience designing traffic control devices and investigating technical design issues.

- Excellent attention to detail, problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.

Company Overview
Noble Built is an Adelaide-based residential construction and property development company specialising in custom home design and construction, residential property development, knockdown and rebuild projects, land subdivision and investment builds. The Company provides comprehensive project services, from initial feasibility assessments, design and council approvals through to construction and final handover. With a focus on quality workmanship, functional design, cost-effective solutions and effective project delivery, Noble Built works with homeowners, landowners and investors to deliver tailored residential projects across Adelaide, South Australia.
About the role
Noble Built is seeking a skilled and experienced Civil Engineering Draftsperson to join our team in Adelaide, South Australia. The successful candidate will be responsible for preparing, developing and modifying detailed civil engineering drawings and technical documentation for residential construction and property development projects. Working closely with project management team, the role will involve preparing engineering drawings based on design requirements and technical specifications, incorporating drawing revisions and ensuring documentation complies with relevant Australian Standards, building codes and local council requirements. This position will play an important role in supporting the preparation of civil engineering documentation and the delivery of the Company's residential projects.
Key Responsibilities
1.           Assisting civil engineer and project supervisor in preparing civil engineering drawings and technical documentation for residential construction, property development and land subdivision projects.
2.           Preparing detailed civil engineering drawings for site layouts, earthworks, site grading, stormwater drainage, sewerage, water supply and associated civil infrastructure works.
3.           Preparing, developing and modifying engineering drawings, sketches and plans in accordance with engineering designs, technical specifications and project requirements.
4.           Preparing technical specifications, drawing schedules and supporting documentation for civil engineering works.
5.           Reviewing survey plans, site measurements and engineering information to ensure the accuracy and completeness of civil engineering drawings.
6.           Using computer-aided design software, including AutoCAD and Civil 3D, to produce, update and revise detailed engineering drawings.
7.           Conducting site inspections, where required, to verify site conditions and identify discrepancies between engineering drawings and actual site conditions.
8.           Liaising with civil engineer and project supervisor regarding technical drawings, design revisions and construction requirements.
About You
- Diploma or higher qualification in Civil Engineering, Civil Engineering Drafting, or a related field.
- Minimum 3 years of relevant experience as a Civil Engineering Draftsperson, preferably within the residential construction or property development industry.
- Proficiency in AutoCAD and Civil 3D.
- Experience with Revit is an advantage.
- Sound knowledge of civil engineering drawings, technical specifications, site layouts, earthworks, stormwater drainage and other civil infrastructure works.
- Ability to interpret engineering drawings, survey plans and technical documentation, and prepare accurate and detailed civil engineering drawings.
- Strong attention to detail, with good analytical, problem-solving and time management skills.
- Effective communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to liaise with engineers, construction personnel, subcontractors and project managers.
Why Join US
Opportunity to work on a diverse range of residential construction and property development projects across Adelaide.
Gain exposure to different stages of residential development, from initial planning and design documentation through to construction.
Work closely with experienced engineer professionals and project management teams.
Develop your technical drafting skills and industry knowledge through hands-on project experience.
Join a collaborative team that values technical accuracy, quality workmanship and professional development.
Be part of a growing business with ongoing residential construction and development projects.

bullets: Join a growing Industry leader and be part of Australia's renewable future

candidates.content_text:
Company Description
Who Are CPP? 
CPP is a leading high-voltage infrastructure provider, connecting renewable energy projects to Australia’s electricity grid.
As a member of Quanta Services, a Fortune 500 company ranked #192 on the NYSX, we specialise in the design, construction, commissioning, and maintenance of substations, transmission lines, wind farms, and battery storage systems.
Established in 1996, we’ve connected more wind farms and renewable batteries than any other company. With over 700 employees and offices in Adelaide, Melbourne, Sydney, and Brisbane, we partner with Australia’s major transmission providers to deliver innovative, end-to-end solutions.
Join us in shaping the future of energy.
CPP Civil
CPP have a dedicated in-house Civil construction department that plays a critical role in project delivery, providing scoping, estimating, management, and construction of civil works across transmission lines, renewables, and utility projects—giving us greater control over key project components.
Our capabilities include access tracks, roads, structural foundations, cable trenches, conduits, oil containment, and site infrastructure such as laydown areas and facilities. We also manage bulk earthworks, drainage, fencing, and signage, ensuring seamless integration of civil works into every project we deliver.
Job Description
We are seeking a Civil Project Engineer to join our rapidly growing team.
In this role, you will support the delivery of high-voltage projects by assisting with project management, contributing to civil design development (primary and/or secondary), supporting procurement, and providing on-site construction and commissioning assistance. You will also be involved in implementing quality systems, preparing ITPs/ITCs, assisting with tendering, reporting, and ensuring all civil construction works are delivered on time, within budget, and to specification. This position provides critical operational support to both Project Managers and Site Managers throughout the project lifecycle.
Qualifications
To be successful in this role, you will possess:
- Demonstrated experience as a Civil Project Engineer on High Voltage construction, particularly BESS or Substation projects.
- Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering
- Working knowledge of the High Voltage infrastructure industry, including project management, design, procurement, construction and commissioning knowledge
- Knowledge of MS Project and Project Management principles
- High level of attention to detail
- Proven ability to work in a team environment and communicate effectively with various stakeholders
- The ability to solve problems and make good decisions in a timely manner, consulting others when appropriate
Additional Information
Be rewarded at CPP.
At CPP, we value our people above all else. We’re dedicated to investing in and developing your talent to help you reach your full potential. By joining us, you’ll have the opportunity to work on industry-leading projects and access the latest technologies. We foster a culture of innovation and welcome fresh ideas – if you're ready to challenge the status quo, we want you to be part of our team.
Benefits include:
Above-market salary package with annual reviews
Annual bonus, discretionary based on individual and business performance
Paid overtime & Travel and Meals Allowance
We offer flexible working options, with the ability to work from home
Access to study assistance for continuous development, and a strong focus on internal promotions to help you grow within
14 weeks paid primary carer's leave & 4 weeks paid secondary carer's leave
Up to 2 weeks of purchased leave
Choice between an iPhone or Samsung mobile + an iPad
On site car parking
Generous employee referral program up to $4,000
Access to an extensive benefits and discounts program with savings at over 400 retailers
Free Employee Assistance Program for you and your family, supporting physical, mental, and financial wellbeing
How to Apply:
To submit an application please upload your resume via the links provided.
For further information, please reach out to jbales@conpower.com.au however applications will not be accepted via email. 
CPP is an equal opportunity employer that fosters a culture of achievement, personal development and offers a diverse, safe and supportive work environment.

candidates.content_text:
About Us
Mornington Peninsula Shire is Victoria's destination municipality, characterised by unique townships, highly productive agriculture, world renowned landscapes, tourist regions, and areas of national and international conservation significance within a vital Green Wedge.
The Shire is responsible for a broad range of infrastructure and community services that support the wellbeing and prosperity of our diverse community. With approximately 1,000 employees, it is a busy and vibrant workplace.
What’s on Offer
 - Culture – Positive, fun and inclusive work environment that is underpinned by our core values which are integral to everything we do. These are Integrity, Openness, Courage, Respect, and Excellence.
 - Opportunity– Casual roles available in our Infrastructure Projects and Engineering services Unit and our Traffic and Transport team, Band 3 - $34.95 per hour, plus 25% casual loading (excl. super).
 - Career – Opportunity to grow and develop with excellent learning and development opportunities.
 - Job Satisfaction – Have a meaningful impact on the community by contributing to achieve positive outcomes across the Mornington Peninsula Shire 
About the Role
The purpose of the Undergraduate Engineer is to support Council’s Infrastructure Projects and Engineering services unit and Traffic and Transport Team. A wide variety of tasks are required to be completed across the units to assist during periods of university holidays as well as throughout the year on free days from Studies, hours will be open to negotiation.
As an Undergraduate Engineer – Projects and Engineering Services, this position aims to provide valuable support to the Project Delivery team to deliver capital works projects, provide assistance to the Development Engineering team and support the Asset Protection team. The Undergraduate Engineer will be rotated through the Development Engineering team, located in Mornington, and the Infrastructure Projects - Project Management team and Asset Protection team, located in Rosebud.
As an Undergraduate Engineer – Traffic & Transport, you will help plan and deliver traffic, parking and road safety initiatives that improve how people move around our townships. You will thrive in this role if you are customer-centric, detail-focused and enjoy turning data and community feedback into practical engineering solutions. 
Reporting to the Team Leader – Civil and Open Space, core responsibilities include:
 - Assist experienced engineers across a range of projects
 - Contribute to technical tasks, analysis and documentation
 - Prepare and review project documents and information
 - Carry out research and background work as needed
 - Help keep records and project details organised
 - Take part in site visits and fieldwork where appropriate
 - Learn how projects are delivered from start to finish
Reporting to the Team Leader- Traffic & Transport, core responsibilities include:
 - Support experienced traffic engineers and planners across a range of projects
 - Collect and process traffic data (counts, surveys, travel times)
 - Help prepare traffic reports, technical notes and traffic management plans
 - Research standards, guidelines and past project information
 - Join site visits, surveys and fieldwork
 - Receive mentoring and regular feedback, with your work reviewed by senior staff
 - Build a foundation for a career in traffic and transport engineering
About You
 - Currently undertaking/studying an Engineering degree at a tertiary level.
 - High level of computer literacy.
 - A current driver’s license.
 - Experience in local government or other complex organisations is desirable
 - An understanding of the Mornington Peninsula townships with local knowledge preferred.
How to Apply
If this role sounds like you, click 'Apply'.
The Mornington Peninsula Shire is committed to creating a diverse and safe environment. We are proud to be an equal opportunity and Child Safe employer. We encourage applications from First Nations people, culturally and linguistically diverse people, people with disabilities, neurodiverse people, and people of all genders, sexualities and age groups.
Mornington Peninsula Shire undertakes a variety of employment screening checks.  This includes employment references, Working with Children Checks and Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check (NCCHC). 
Applicants must have valid Australian work rights.
For further information about the role, you can download the Position Description by clicking 'Apply'. For a confidential discussion about this opportunity, please contact: Marios Antoniou, Graduate Development Engineer, 03 5950 1248.
Applications Close: 11:59pm, Friday 27 November 2026.

candidates.content_text:
Excavation, Piling, Shoring and Structural Civil Works
Dig It Pty Ltd is seeking an experienced Civil Estimator to price excavation, shoring, piling and structural civil packages for builders across Sydney.
This is an office-based role in Mascot for an estimator with around 5 years of civil estimating experience and a background with Tier 2 builders or contractors. You will take tenders from enquiry through to submission and produce the BOQs our site teams build and are measured against.
You will be pricing projects involving:
- Bulk and detailed excavation
- Basement excavation and rock removal
- Piling and shoring
- Anchors and capping beams
- Shotcrete
- Formwork, reinforcement and structural concrete
- Demolition and remediation
- Cartage, spoil classification and disposal
About Us
A highly regarded Sydney-based civil contractor, in the industry for 20+ years. Delivering excavation, piling, shoring, structural concrete and early works packages for builders, developers and private clients.
We undertake technically challenging projects where planning, accurate pricing and practical construction knowledge are critical.
We operate our own fleet of excavators, trucks and civil plant and have a strong pipeline of secured work across Sydney.
The role
You will report to our Project Coordinator, take part in the weekly estimating meeting and work closely with our site team and management.
Your responsibilities will include:
- Reviewing tender documents, architectural, structural and shoring drawings, specifications and geotechnical reports
- Preparing quantity take-offs for excavation, rock, piling, shoring, shotcrete, anchors, capping beams and concrete works
- Building first principles estimates for labour, plant, cartage, tipping, materials and subcontractors
- Preparing clear BOQs, methodology and inclusions/exclusions for builder clients
- Obtaining and comparing subcontractor and supplier pricing
- Identifying risks, assumptions and opportunities in each tender
- Managing several tenders at once and meeting submission deadlines
- Following up submitted quotes with clients
- Handing over won jobs to the project team with a clear scope and budget
- Pricing variations as required
About you
You will be accurate, organised and commercially minded, with a practical understanding of how the work is built on site.
You should have:
- Around 5 years of estimating experience in civil construction
- Tier 2 experience, either estimating for a Tier 2 contractor or pricing packages for Tier 2 builders
- Strong knowledge of excavation, shoring and piling methods and construction sequencing
- The ability to read civil, structural and shoring drawings and geotechnical reports
- Experience estimating rock, spoil classification and disposal costs
- Strong Excel skills and experience with take-off software (e.g. CostX, Bluebeam or similar)
- Good written communication for tender submissions and client correspondence
- Full Australian working rights
Site experience and a civil engineering or construction qualification will be highly regarded.
What we offer
- $120,000 base salary
- Superannuation paid in addition to the base salary
- Permanent, long-term employment
- Strong pipeline of secured Sydney projects
- Direct access to company management
- Technically challenging and varied civil projects
- Opportunity to progress into a senior estimating role
How to apply
Submit your CV together with a brief summary of the civil packages you have estimated, including the types and values of projects.

candidates.content_text:
About BMD
BMD is Australia’s leading integrated engineering, construction and urban development business, with foundations built on the family values that underpin our unique, collaborative approach. Driven by a purpose of powering futures and creating enduring legacies through a commitment to collaboration, BMD is delivering infrastructure solutions that connect and transform communities. With a proud history beginning in 1979, BMD now employs 2,400 people throughout Australia, the Philippines and United Kingdom.
About the Role
As part of the delivery of the Gateway to Bruce Highway Upgrade, BMD is seeking a Site Engineer to join the project team on one of Southeast Queensland's most significant transport infrastructure projects. Reporting to the Project Manager, you will provide onsite engineering and technical support across major motorway upgrade works between Bracken Ridge and Pine River, helping deliver improved capacity, safety and connectivity along this critical transport corridor. You will play a key role in coordinating construction activities, managing subcontractors, monitoring quality outcomes and supporting the successful delivery of complex civil infrastructure works.
This role operates on a 5/2 roster, with occasional Saturday work required to support project delivery. The position is best suited to candidates based in Brisbane or those willing to relocate to the area, as it is a local project with no FIFO arrangements.
Key Responsibilities
- Provide onsite engineering support to construction teams
- Assist with day‑to‑day coordination of subcontractors and site activities
- Set out works and verify construction against design and specifications
- Support quality assurance, inspections and documentation processes
- Assist with short‑term planning, progress tracking and reporting
- Promote strong safety, environmental and quality outcomes on site
- Work closely with Project Engineers, Site Supervisors and subcontractors
Skills and Experience
- Bachelor’s degree in Civil or Structural Engineering
- Minimum two years working onsite on civil infrastructure projects 
- Exposure to earthworks, structures, roads or related scopes preferred
- Strong attention to detail with a proactive, solutions‑focused mindset
Diversity and inclusion
We recognise that we are strengthened by diversity, and we embrace differences as an equal opportunity employer providing a flexible and inclusive workplace.
So, join our team, be yourself and help us power futures and create legacies. 
We’re a purpose and values-led business guided by our values of family, empowered, collaborative and driven. For further details on what makes BMD unique, head to https://www.bmdgroup.global/careers

candidates.abstract: We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Structural Revit Cadet to join our dynamic Bridge Team.
candidates.content_text:
Work with Us. Change the World.
At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.
There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.
We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.
Job Description
At AECOM, we’re passionate about shaping the future of infrastructure. Our Bridge Team is at the forefront of designing and delivering innovative, sustainable, and resilient bridge structures that connect communities and improve lives. Join us and be part of a global network of professionals dedicated to making a difference.
We are seeking a motivated and enthusiastic Structural Revit Cadet to join our dynamic Bridge Team. This is an exciting opportunity to kickstart your career in structural engineering and gain hands-on experience with cutting-edge tools and technologies. You’ll work alongside industry leaders and contribute to impactful projects that shape the built environment.
How you’ll make a difference:
- Assist in creating detailed 3D models and technical drawings using Revit software for bridge and structural projects.  
- Collaborate with engineers and designers to develop accurate and efficient designs.  
- Support the preparation of project documentation, including plans, schedules, and reports.
- Participate in team meetings, site visits, and project reviews.  
- Learn and apply industry standards, codes, and best practices in bridge design and drafting.
Qualifications
About You
We’re looking for a proactive and eager learner who is passionate about structural engineering and design. To be successful in this role, you’ll need:  
- Education: Currently enrolled or studying an Associate Degree or advanced Diploma in Civil Engineering, Structural Engineering, or a related field.  
- Software Skills: Basic knowledge of Revit is essential; experience with AutoCAD or other design software is a plus.  
- Attention to Detail: Strong focus on accuracy and quality in design and documentation.  
- Team Player: Excellent communication and collaboration skills to work effectively in a team environment.  
- Willingness to Learn: A positive attitude and eagerness to develop new skills and grow within the field.
Why Join AECOM? 
- Mentorship & Training: Learn from experienced professionals and gain hands-on experience in real-world projects.  
- Career Growth: Build a strong foundation for your career in structural engineering and bridge design.  
- Innovation & Impact: Be part of projects that make a difference in communities around the world.  
- Inclusive Culture: Join a supportive and diverse team that values collaboration and creativity.
Additional Information
- Submit Your Application: Complete the job application, uploading your resume, cover letter and the latest copy of your academic transcripts as one single document.  
- Phone Screen: You may be invited to a phone screen with our Early Careers Recruitment team.  
- Interview: Attend a face-to-face interview at your local office.  
Applications are reviewed as they come in, and the role may close earlier than expected, so if this opportunity sounds like you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.
